title: Patrol Hours: see who is actually turning up
changes: New: the bot now counts how long your officers spend in patrol voice channels. Run /duty to see your own hours, or /patrolboard to see the whole server ranked
It is already counting. Recording is free on every server and starts as soon as you have patrol channels set, so by the time you look there is real history there rather than an empty page

The number is meant to survive an argument. Time spent deafened does not count, sitting in a channel on your own does not count at all, and one shift is capped at 6 hours, so nobody tops the board by leaving Discord open overnight
With Premium: the 30 and 90 day views, every officer instead of the top 10, a board that posts itself in a channel every week, and a list of who has not been on patrol in 14 days
Nobody on that list gets messaged by the bot. It tells you, and what happens next is your call
Set it up with /config dutytime, or on the dashboard. It counts from the same patrol channels dispatch already uses

Free servers can set up voice dispatch from /config dispatch again. That screen was turning them away even though /setup and the dashboard both let them through, and the 911 announcements it gates are meant to be free
Applications are no longer Premium only. Every server gets 2 application types, and Premium removes the limit

If your server uses the Priority Tracker, the web CAD now shows it in the top corner for everyone, civilians and LEO and fire alike. It says whether a priority is running and how long is left on the cooldown, and updates on its own
